subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: Prove that C₀ + C₁/2 + C₂/3 + … + Cₙ/(n + 1) = (2ⁿ⁺¹ − 1)/(n + 1).

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — what you multiply the sum by and why, which identity raises the index to n + 1, what the new sum adds up to, and how you divide back.
insider_note: After the identity the sum starts at ⁿ⁺¹C₁, so it is 2ⁿ⁺¹ − 1, not 2ⁿ⁺¹. The −1 in the answer is the missing ⁿ⁺¹C₀ = 1 — forget it and the last two marks are gone.

steps.label: Write the sum with ⁿCᵣ
steps.margin_note: First mark. This is the x-series with x = 1: every term is ⁿCᵣ divided by r + 1.
steps.memory_tip: Every denominator is r + 1, one more than the index. This is the x-series with x = 1.
lines: Let S = C₀ + C₁/2 + C₂/3 + … + Cₙ/(n + 1)

recall.must_convey: That the sum is named S and each Cᵣ is written as ⁿCᵣ with denominator r + 1.
accept: let S be the sum and write each C r as n C r over r plus one
S equals n C nought plus half n C one plus a third n C two and so on
name the left side S with the binomial coefficients n C r
sum ni S ani pettukoni C r ni n C r by r plus one ga rayali
each term is n C r over r plus one

steps.why: Naming the left side S and writing Cᵣ as ⁿCᵣ makes the index n visible, and n is what the next step changes into n + 1.
common_mistakes: Reading the denominators as r instead of r + 1.

steps.label: Multiply by n + 1
steps.margin_note: Second and third marks. Multiplying by n + 1 puts (n + 1)/(r + 1) in front of each ⁿCᵣ — no x this time.
steps.memory_tip: Multiplying by n + 1 puts (n + 1)/(r + 1) in front of each ⁿCᵣ. No x in this version.

recall.must_convey: That multiplying S by n + 1 gives terms ((n + 1)/(r + 1))·ⁿCᵣ.
accept: multiply by n plus one so each term has n plus one by r plus one in front
n plus one S equals n plus one by one n C nought plus n plus one by two n C one and so on
multiply both sides by n plus one
n plus one tho multiply cheste prathi term lo n plus one by r plus one vasthundi
the factor n plus one over r plus one appears in every term
heard_as: n plus one by r plus one

steps.why: The denominators 1, 2, 3, …, n + 1 are the r + 1 in ((n + 1)/(r + 1))·ⁿCᵣ. Multiplying by n + 1 makes each term exactly that identity.
common_mistakes: Multiplying only the left side by n + 1.

steps.label: Use ((n + 1)/(r + 1))·ⁿCᵣ = ⁿ⁺¹Cᵣ₊₁
steps.margin_note: Fourth and fifth marks. ((n + 1)/(r + 1))·ⁿCᵣ = ⁿ⁺¹Cᵣ₊₁ — one row down, one index along. Every term of the sum becomes a coefficient of (1 + x)ⁿ⁺¹.
steps.memory_tip: ((n + 1)/(r + 1))·ⁿCᵣ = ⁿ⁺¹Cᵣ₊₁ — one row down, one index along. The sum now starts at ⁿ⁺¹C₁.

recall.must_convey: That each ((n + 1)/(r + 1))·ⁿCᵣ becomes ⁿ⁺¹Cᵣ₊₁, so (n + 1)S = ⁿ⁺¹C₁ + ⁿ⁺¹C₂ + … + ⁿ⁺¹Cₙ₊₁.
accept: n plus one by r plus one times n C r is n plus one C r plus one so the sum becomes n plus one C one plus n plus one C two and so on
raise the index to n plus one with the identity
each term becomes a coefficient of one plus x to the n plus one
identity vadithe prathi term n plus one C r plus one avthundi
the coefficients become n plus one C one up to n plus one C n plus one
heard_as: n plus one C r plus one
n plus one by r plus one

steps.why: Once every term is ⁿ⁺¹Cᵣ₊₁, the whole sum is the sum of the coefficients of (1 + x)ⁿ⁺¹ with its first term missing — which is what putting x = 1 in the expansion gives.
common_mistakes: Forgetting that the sum now starts at ⁿ⁺¹C₁, not ⁿ⁺¹C₀.

steps.label: Sum the expansion and divide
steps.margin_note: Sixth and seventh marks. ⁿ⁺¹C₀ + ⁿ⁺¹C₁ + … + ⁿ⁺¹Cₙ₊₁ = 2ⁿ⁺¹, and ⁿ⁺¹C₀ = 1 is missing, so the sum is 2ⁿ⁺¹ − 1.
steps.memory_tip: All the coefficients of (1 + x)ⁿ⁺¹ add to 2ⁿ⁺¹, and ⁿ⁺¹C₀ = 1 is missing — hence the −1.

recall.must_convey: That the sum equals 2ⁿ⁺¹ − 1, so S = (2ⁿ⁺¹ − 1)/(n + 1).
accept: the sum of all the coefficients is two to the n plus one, minus the missing one, divide by n plus one
n plus one S equals two to the n plus one minus one
S equals two to the n plus one minus one over n plus one
coefficients sum two power n plus one minus one, n plus one tho divide cheste S vasthundi
sum of the binomial coefficients of one plus x to the n plus one is two to the n plus one
heard_as: two to the n plus one

steps.why: ⁿ⁺¹C₁ + ⁿ⁺¹C₂ + … + ⁿ⁺¹Cₙ₊₁ is 2ⁿ⁺¹ minus its first term ⁿ⁺¹C₀ = 1. Dividing back by what was multiplied gives S.
common_mistakes: Writing the sum of the coefficients as 2ⁿ instead of 2ⁿ⁺¹.
Forgetting the −1 for the missing ⁿ⁺¹C₀.
